title: App Mafia: Blake Anderson on controversy, power-law bets and focusing on the core app funnel
summary: A loose, banter-heavy podcast with the App Mafia founders. Blake's useful points: use controversy to gain reach and hiring leverage, focus only on the few funnel metrics that matter, take asymmetric bets, and push through self-doubt. Much of the episode is jokes and lifestyle talk with little durable insight.

principles.text: Ego preservation stops you taking controversial risks that would build influence.
principles.quote: ego preservation that leads us to to not take risks and not do things that are controversial that are that that would enable us to gain influence

principles.text: Algorithmic reach and distribution let you hire higher quality talent.
principles.quote: The more algorithmic reach and distribution that you have, the higher quality talent that you can attract.

principles.text: Obsess over the few core app funnel steps (download, convert, retain); everything else can wait.
principles.quote: identify the core uh components of the business, getting people to download, converting them, making sure that they have a good experience and that they stay.

principles.text: Treat business risks as power laws: take bets with a decent floor and a multi-million upside every time.
principles.quote: okay, we think that at like minimum we're going to get $300,000 back from this 500k that we spend. Um, you know, uh accounting for direct response as well as word of mouth, but upside is in the range of millions, right?

principles.text: Bootstrapping makes every bet personal because the spend comes out of your own pocket.
principles.quote: that's actually probably one of the biggest downsides to bootstrapping is that because it is your money, every dollar that you spend is coming out of your pocket.

principles.text: The hardest obstacle for a founder is self-doubt before external proof arrives.
principles.quote: the hardest thing that I've ever ever overcome was doubt.
